chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdī, from Muhammad ibn Khallād al-Sayqal, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I was seated in the presence of ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad in al-Madīnah, and I had stayed with him for two years, writing from him what he heard from his brother, meaning Abā al-Hasan عليه السلام, when Abū Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام entered the mosque, the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله. Then ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar sprang up without shoes and without a cloak, kissed his hand, and honored him. So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him, “O uncle, sit down, may Allah have mercy on you.” He said, “O my master, how can I sit while you are standing?”

Then when ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar returned to his gathering, his companions began reproaching him and saying, “You are the uncle of his father, and you do this to him?” He said, “Be silent. If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not deemed this white hair worthy, and has deemed this young man worthy, and placed him where He placed him, should I deny his merit? We seek refuge in Allah from what you are saying. Rather, I am his servant.”

key_terms.سَيِّدِي: my master; a term of reverence and acknowledgment of rank
key_terms.عَبْدٌ: servant or slave; expressing complete humility before the Imam
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him; an honorific used for the Imam
key_terms.فَضْلَهُ: his merit or excellence, recognized as divinely granted
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الرَّسُولِ: the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, the setting of the encounter
key_terms.نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ: we seek refuge in Allah; an expression of dissociation from improper speech

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar demonstrate recognition of the Imam’s divinely appointed status?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar showed profound reverence to Imam Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام despite being older and from the previous generation. It highlights recognition of divinely granted rank and merit, showing that true authority and excellence are based on Allah’s designation rather than age or family seniority.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Khallad Al Sayqal, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ammar who said,

‘I was seated in the presence of Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Medina, and I was staying with him for two years, writing from him what he had heard from his brother<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) when Abu Ja’far Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> entered the Masjid, the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So Ali Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> leapt up without any shoes nor a robe, and he kissed his<sup>asws</sup> hand and revered him<sup>asws</sup>. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to him, ‘O Uncle, be seated, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you’. So he said, ‘O my Chief<sup>asws</sup>! How can I sit while you<sup>asws</sup> are standing?’

So when Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> returned to his gathering, his companions went on rebuking him and they were saying, ‘You are an uncle of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, and you are doing this deed with him<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he said, ‘Be silent! When it was so that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’, and he grabbed his own beard, ‘has not Sanctified this old man and has Sanctified this youth, and Placed him<sup>asws</sup> where He<sup>azwj</sup> Placed him<sup>asws</sup>, (how can I) deny his<sup>asws</sup> merits? I seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from what you are saying. But, I am a slave of his<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 12. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Muhammad ibn Khallad al.-Sayqal from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following.

“Once I was in a meeting with Ali ibn Ja‘far ibn Muhammad in Madina, - I stayed with him for two years to write from him what he would hear from his brother, abu al-Hassan (a.s.),- at such time abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.) came in the mosque, the mosque of the Messenger of Allah. Ali ibn Ja‘far rushed towards him bare foot and without his gown. He kissed his hand and showed great respect for him. Abu Ja‘far said to him, “Uncle, please sit down, may Allah grant you well being.” He said, “My master, how can I sit when you are standing.”

When Ali ibn Ja‘far returned to his place his companions began to blame him saying, “You are the uncle of his father, how can you act as such before him?” He said to them, “Be quite, When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, has not qualified this beard –holding his beard in his hand- but has qualified this young man and has given him such position, should I deny his excellence and virtue? I seek refuge before Allah from what you say. In fact, I am a servant for him.”
